audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and packet chart read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Hwei/Hwei.
audit.why: Hwei out-ranges Blooming Burst (800) and Tangle-Barbs (1000) with QQ; the only stage Neeko genuinely contests is 6, when Pop Blossom's hidden wind-up gives her an opener Hwei cannot dash out of.
audit.corrected: Sides moved to match the packet and content chart, level 6 left as Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Multiple fields describe a 'W leap', a 'W leap-stun combo', and 'diving your backline with W and R'. Shapesplitter (W) is not a leap — it is a clone plus a third-attack damage and move-speed passive. The leap is Pop Blossom (R).
audit.why: Riot's W text: bonus magic damage every third attack with brief move speed, activate to send a clone, recast to redirect it. Riot's R text: after a short preparation she leaps into the air, knocking up nearby enemies, then damages and stuns on landing.
audit.corrected: Every 'W leap' reference re-pointed to Pop Blossom, with its real 600 range and 120/105/90 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly told you to 'sidestep it behind minions' for Tangle-Barbs. Tangle-Barbs roots everything it passes through, so minions do not stop it — and passing through a champion makes it larger, faster and longer-rooting.
audit.why: Riot's E text is explicit: it damages and roots everything it passes through, and grows if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion. Hiding behind a minion wave is not counterplay; stepping laterally out of the line is.
audit.corrected: cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5], winCon and tradeBad now say to dodge laterally and note that the root passes through minions and grows on champion hits.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and winCon referenced a 'fifteen-second gap' that matches nothing in Neeko's kit.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, Blooming Burst 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Shapesplitter 16-12, Pop Blossom 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, winCon, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour's effect on the ultimate was never stated: the Pop Blossom preparation is hidden while Neeko is disguised.
audit.why: Riot's R text ends with 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' Against an immobile champion with no dash, that is the single most dangerous thing in the matchup — the usual visual tell is simply absent.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2].d and spikes[1].text.

edits.before: Neeko's early poke relies on landing Q reliably, which your E-Q combo out-damages and outranges through the laning phase. Her disguise tricks can bait a bad trade if you're careless, so play around wards and don't blindly walk up on suspicious minions or allies. Through levels 1-4 you should be winning most direct trades as long as you respect her W leap-stun combo rather than standing still.

edits.before: Level 6 is a genuine skill check - her ultimate lets her dive straight onto you from range, and if she lands the initial stun she can chain into a real kill threat. Keep your escape options open and don't overextend on poke alone once she's 6, since her all-in punishes greed hard. Outside of her all-in window your ranged combo and wave control still keep you ahead through levels 4-5.
